options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor is monotone sequentially complete: every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Audit the precise relationship between normality of the projection lattice and monotone sequential completeness. Look for a valid argument transferring suprema of increasing projections to suprema of arbitrary bounded increasing self-adjoint sequences.

options.approach: Revisit bounded graph-operator constructions in the matrix algebra M_2(M). Investigate whether the complete projection lattice can encode the entire increasing sequence as compatible graph subspaces and produce its least upper bound.

options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor is monotone sequentially complete: every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Investigate whether quasitracial completeness, together with monotonicity, forces bounded increasing sequences to be quasitrace-metric Cauchy. Establishing that implication would produce a supremum without assuming that the quasitrace is additive.

options.counterfactual: There exists at least one finite AW*-factor satisfying all the requirements in the definition of G for some positive increment.
options.approach: Start with a hypothetical witness and investigate transformations that increase its constant increment while preserving boundedness. Use corners, matrix amplification, and normalization by positive upper bounds to seek a sharp attainable endpoint.

options.counterfactual: The quasitracial ultraproduct argument does not establish that G contains its positive supremum, so a nonempty G could have an excluded endpoint.
options.approach: Audit whether the quasitracial ultraproduct is necessarily an AW*-factor under exactly the stated hypotheses. Check projection lifting, arbitrary projection joins, factoriality, and the extension of the quasitrace to two-by-two matrices separately.

options.approach: Audit the saturation argument intended to exclude a least upper bound in the ultraproduct. Check that the order constraints and the positive-part quasitrace constraint are uniformly continuous in the relevant metric and jointly realizable.

options.approach: Avoid saturation and attempt a coordinatewise diagonal construction of an upper bound contradicting any proposed least upper bound. This would distinguish a genuine endpoint obstruction from a gap in the model-theoretic argument.
